candidate.blueprint_locator: 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan, Health Promotion and Maintenance, printed p.9 / PDF p.13
candidate.educational_objective: Use all components of the current CDC child/adolescent immunization schedule when making vaccine recommendations.

options.A: Use the age table only and ignore catch-up intervals, medical indications, notes, and contraindications
options.B: Determine recommendations by age, then review catch-up intervals, medical indications, notes, and contraindications/precautions
options.C: Restart every vaccine series whenever a child is behind schedule
options.D: Choose vaccines only from the parent’s preferred timing without consulting the schedule

candidate.rationale: The current CDC schedule directs healthcare professionals to determine vaccines by age, review catch-up intervals, assess additional recommendations by medical indication, review notes for intervals and special situations, and review contraindications and precautions.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Healthcare providers should use the age table, catch-up table, medical-indication table, notes, and contraindications/precautions when making recommendations.
candidate.source_document_title: Child and Adolescent Immunization Schedule by Age (Addendum updated July 2, 2025)
candidate.source_locator: Purpose and How to use the schedule, steps 1–5
candidate.source_version_date: July 2, 2025 schedule; currently operative in 2026 pursuant to the March 16, 2026 preliminary court order
candidate.stem: A nurse is using the current CDC Child and Adolescent Immunization Schedule to make a vaccine recommendation. Which approach follows the schedule correctly?
